$comment: Normative (FLR-ADR-006). The `default` keywords here are exactly the constant defaults of 17.1's and 17.2's tables; the reference canonicalizer reads them as its table of constant defaults (9.2 step 1).
title: Stair
description: 17.1: a stair between two levels of a building — where it starts, the way it rises, its width, tread, riser count or greatest riser height, form, handrail and the headroom it is designed for. It has only the members of its table (FS-CORE-17.1.1), and exactly one of `risers` and `maxRiser`. That its `level` and `to` resolve (FS-CORE-3.2.1) and are two levels of one building (FS-CORE-17.1.2), that its rise is greater than zero (FS-CORE-17.4.1) and that its riser count fits its form (FS-CORE-17.4.2) are invariants, not checked here.

level.description: 17.1: a reference to the level the stair rises from; its foot is on it. Always present.

to.description: 17.1: a reference to the level the stair rises to; its head is on it. Always present.

position.description: 17.1, 17.3: the middle of the stair's first nosing line, in plan: the origin of its frame. Always present.

rotation.description: 17.1, 17.3: the direction the first flight rises in, counter-clockwise from +X; its frame faces F(rotation) (13.1).

width.description: 17.1: the stair's width, greater than zero (FS-CORE-17.1.1). Always present.

tread.description: 17.1: the going — the horizontal distance from one nosing to the next, along the walkline — greater than zero (FS-CORE-17.1.1). Always present.

risers.description: 17.1, 17.4: the number of risers from the foot to the head, an integer from 1 to 2^53 − 1 (FS-CORE-17.1.1). Absent: derived from maxRiser (17.4); a stair has exactly one of risers and maxRiser.

maxRiser.description: 17.1, 17.4: the greatest riser height the stair may have; its riser count is the least that keeps every riser no higher (17.4). Greater than zero (FS-CORE-17.1.1). Absent: the stair has risers.

minHeadroom.description: 17.1, 17.6: the least headroom the stair is designed to have: what the opening it needs in the floor above is cut for (17.6). Greater than zero (FS-CORE-17.1.3). Absent: none is declared, and no opening is derived. New in 0.4.

handrail.description: 17.1: the stair's handrail. Absent: no handrail is declared.

option.description: 19.2: a reference to the option this stair is in. Absent: it is in no option, and so in every design.

name.description: 1.4: a human-readable label, 1–200 characters. Absent by default.

form.title: Stair form
form.description: 17.2: a stair's form, exactly one of five (FS-CORE-17.2.1); a winder stair turns a quarter or a half. That a spiral stair's width is at most half its diameter (FS-CORE-17.2.2) is an invariant (FS-INV-904), not checked here. A winder stair may have a newel (0.4).

oneOf.title: L-shaped stair
oneOf.description: 17.2: { "kind": "lShaped", "turn", "risersBeforeTurn" } — two flights at right angles, joined by a square landing.

turn.description: 17.2: the way the stair turns as it is walked up: "left" is counter-clockwise seen from above.

risersBeforeTurn.description: 17.2: the number of risers of the first flight, the last of which rises onto the landing or the first winder; an integer from 1 to 2^53 − 1 (FS-CORE-17.2.1). That the stair's riser count fits it (FS-CORE-17.4.2) is an invariant (FS-INV-903), not checked here. Always present.

oneOf.title: U-shaped stair
oneOf.description: 17.2: { "kind": "uShaped", "turn", "risersBeforeTurn", "gap"? } — two parallel flights joined by a landing across both.

turn.description: 17.2: the way the stair turns as it is walked up: "left" is counter-clockwise seen from above.

risersBeforeTurn.description: 17.2: the number of risers of the first flight, the last of which rises onto the landing or the first winder; an integer from 1 to 2^53 − 1 (FS-CORE-17.2.1). That the stair's riser count fits it (FS-CORE-17.4.2) is an invariant (FS-INV-903), not checked here. Always present.

gap.description: 17.2: the distance between the two flights, in plan; not negative (FS-CORE-17.2.1).

oneOf.title: Quarter-turn winder stair
oneOf.description: 17.2: { "kind": "winder", "angle": "quarter", "turn", "risersBeforeTurn", "winders", "newel"? } — an L that turns on winders; it has no gap (FS-CORE-17.2.1).

turn.description: 17.2: the way the stair turns as it is walked up: "left" is counter-clockwise seen from above.

risersBeforeTurn.description: 17.2: the number of risers of the first flight, the last of which rises onto the landing or the first winder; an integer from 1 to 2^53 − 1 (FS-CORE-17.2.1). That the stair's riser count fits it (FS-CORE-17.4.2) is an invariant (FS-INV-903), not checked here. Always present.

winders.description: 17.2: the number of winder treads at the turn, an integer from 1 to 2^53 − 1 (FS-CORE-17.2.1). Always present.

newel.description: 17.2, 17.7: the depth of the newel at the inner side of the turn, on whose faces the winders' narrow ends stand; greater than zero (FS-CORE-17.2.3). That it lies inside the circle of the walkline (FS-CORE-17.7.4) is an invariant (FS-INV-905), not checked here. Absent: there is no newel, and the winders meet at the pivot of the turn. New in 0.4.

oneOf.title: Half-turn winder stair
oneOf.description: 17.2: { "kind": "winder", "angle": "half", "turn", "risersBeforeTurn", "winders", "gap"?, "newel"? } — a U that turns on winders.

turn.description: 17.2: the way the stair turns as it is walked up: "left" is counter-clockwise seen from above.

risersBeforeTurn.description: 17.2: the number of risers of the first flight, the last of which rises onto the landing or the first winder; an integer from 1 to 2^53 − 1 (FS-CORE-17.2.1). That the stair's riser count fits it (FS-CORE-17.4.2) is an invariant (FS-INV-903), not checked here. Always present.

winders.description: 17.2: the number of winder treads at the turn, an integer from 1 to 2^53 − 1 (FS-CORE-17.2.1). Always present.

gap.description: 17.2: the distance between the two flights, in plan; not negative (FS-CORE-17.2.1).

newel.description: 17.2, 17.7: the depth of the newel at the inner side of the turn, on whose faces the winders' narrow ends stand; greater than zero (FS-CORE-17.2.3). That it lies inside the circle of the walkline (FS-CORE-17.7.4) is an invariant (FS-INV-905), not checked here. Absent: there is no newel, and the winders meet at the pivot of the turn. New in 0.4.

oneOf.title: Spiral stair
oneOf.description: 17.2: { "kind": "spiral", "turn", "diameter", "sweep" } — treads that wind around a centre.

turn.description: 17.2: the way the stair turns as it is walked up: "left" is counter-clockwise seen from above.

diameter.description: 17.2: the stair's outer diameter, greater than zero (FS-CORE-17.2.1). Always present.

sweep.description: 17.2, 17.3: the angle, in microdegrees, the stair turns through from its first nosing line to its last: an integer from 1 to 2^53 − 1 (FS-CORE-17.2.1). Always present.

handrail.title: Handrail
handrail.description: 17.1: a stair's handrail, as declared: its height above the nosing line and the sides it is on.

height.description: 17.1: the handrail's height above the nosing line, greater than zero (FS-CORE-17.1.1). Always present.

sides.description: 17.1: the sides of the stair, as walked up, that have a handrail.
